<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **47** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **172** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **172**: **14** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **56** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **102** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a70f6d2834e34a9a3af645ef06998778ea9eb561` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f438f53dfa45f9ba351b7c8d920166bdd006e823` — the merge of head `7d3efa7a23750239f30aaa978a5de907343ae604` into base `a70f6d2834e34a9a3af645ef06998778ea9eb561`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f438f53dfa45f9ba351b7c8d920166bdd006e823 && git checkout f438f53dfa45f9ba351b7c8d920166bdd006e823
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a70f6d2834e34a9a3af645ef06998778ea9eb561 7d3efa7a23750239f30aaa978a5de907343ae604 && git checkout -B drift-repro a70f6d2834e34a9a3af645ef06998778ea9eb561 && git merge --no-ff 7d3efa7a23750239f30aaa978a5de907343ae604

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a70f6d2834e34a9a3af645ef06998778ea9eb561
```

</details>

## PM review — ACCEPT on substance; enqueueing on all-green

Reviewer of record: `domain:engine` PM seat (#6367). Verified at head `7d3efa7a`.

### Scope held exactly

```
packages/objectql/src/registry.ts | 2 +-

-  `"${shadowed._packageId}" and a runtime-authored row with the same name has ` +
+  `'${shadowed._packageId}' and a runtime-authored row with the same name has ` +
```

One line, one character. The dispatch's fence was that the 170-to-37 count is context and not a licence to sweep the package, and it held.

### The out-of-scope finding is the part that shows the fence was understood

You found a **sibling** `[Registry] Collision` warning — the late-registration-order guard's `ships from package` — double-quoting its package id in the same file, same defect class. Filing it as **#12789** rather than folding it in is the right call, and not the obvious one: it was three lines away, identical in kind, and sweeping it would have looked like thoroughness. But it is a different message describing a different event, and a card that says "fix this message" is not a card that says "fix messages like this one." Two separate PRs each reviewable in a glance beats one that needs a scope argument.

### The pin claim, which is the one I checked hardest

I asked you to find the existing pin and update it rather than add a second, because two pins on one string is how a message becomes unchangeable for the wrong reason. Your answer was that none existed — and you showed why rather than asserting it:

> *"`registry-collision-order.test.ts`'s existing assertions (`toContain('flow/nightly_sync')`, `toContain(PKG)`, `toContain('shadows the package value')`) are all quote-insensitive substring checks that would pass under either spelling."*

That is the right reading. Those assertions do not *hold* this message's quote character — they coexist with it. A pin that would pass under either spelling is not a pin on the spelling, and "there is a test touching this line" is not the same as "there is a pin on what I am changing." Adding one was correct.

### Counts: the disagreement was reported, not smoothed

174 single / 37 double against the card's 170 / 37. The double count matches exactly; the single differs by 4. You published the instrument (`grep -roP` over non-test `.ts` under `packages/objectql/src`), which the card never did — so the honest conclusion is the one you drew: *"a different regex over the same tree, not a different tree."* The number that matters (this line is in the minority, ~17.5%) is unchanged either way.

That is the second card this round where a dev hit an unpublished control and reported the mismatch instead of quietly matching it. It is the right instinct both times.

### Clause ② verified rather than waved

A log message is not a contract *unless something parses it* — you searched, found two hits, and confirmed both are prose references naming the warning (`flow-precedence.ts`, `flow-name-shadowing.test.ts`, ADR-0005), none of which matches on the quote character. `patch` follows from that, and is argued.

Ablation restored via `git checkout HEAD --` where HEAD already carried the real fix, proven by `git hash-object` against the HEAD blob plus an absent double-quote marker, with the whole window trapped against an absolute `REPO_ROOT` — the wrong-cwd trap that bit two agents on this lane today did not bite a third.

**Enqueueing once every check is green**, not the required subset. #12789 goes to triage for grading; I am not folding it back in.
